item.title: Cerebras launches CS-4 wafer-scale AI system with up to 30x faster inference than GPUs and modular design for hyperscale deployment [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Cerebras has introduced the CS-4, a new wafer-scale AI system that delivers up to 30 times faster inference compared to GPU systems, targeting hyperscale data centers. The CS-4 features three WSE-3 Turbo wafers per system, enhanced power delivery, cooling, and I/O, and a modular Nexus Platform Architecture designed to simplify manufacturing, deployment, and upgrades. The system achieves higher throughput per watt and reduces wafer-to-wafer interconnect latency to 2 microseconds, enabling interactive performance on models exceeding 10 trillion parameters. Its modular compute backpack design integrates power conversion, cooling, and control electronics into a compact package, reducing deployment time from days to hours. The first CS-4 shipments are expected to begin this quarter.

item.title: Claude generates macOS driver for obscure HP printer originally built only for Windows [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A user reported that Claude, an AI system, successfully wrote a macOS driver for an obscure HP printer that was originally designed to support only Windows. This development enables the printer to function on macOS without official support from HP.

item.title: INXM launches local Rust desktop app using LLM as compiler to create deterministic AI workflows without runtime improvisation [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: INXM has released a local-first Rust desktop application that uses large language models (LLMs) as compilers rather than runtime engines, enabling users to describe intent in chat which is then compiled into typed, validated plans executed deterministically. The app supports plan-owned conversations, reusable typed inputs, human-in-the-loop interactions, and repair loops for failed runs, with a local HTTP server to manage and execute workflows across clients. The application integrates with existing AI agents like Codex and Claude via API keys or local endpoints, and offers a command palette for workflow control. It supports installation on Linux, macOS, and Windows without requiring admin rights, though builds are currently unsigned and may trigger OS security warnings. INXM aims to provide a deterministic, versioned, and repairable AI workflow environment that avoids AI improvisation during execution.

item.title: TerraPower plans to power AI data centers with molten salt-cooled nuclear reactors featuring built-in energy storage for flexible output
item.description: TerraPower, founded by Bill Gates, is developing molten salt-cooled nuclear reactors designed to provide stable and flexible power for AI data centers. The company plans to announce its first data center project this year, with construction expected to start in 2027. TerraPower's reactors store excess heat in molten sodium, allowing rapid power output adjustments without ramping the reactor itself, addressing the fluctuating energy demands of AI workloads. This energy storage capability enables the reactors to complement intermittent renewable sources like wind and solar, offering a high capacity factor and operational flexibility. TerraPower's approach aims to reduce reliance on costly battery banks and natural gas turbines, potentially giving it an advantage in securing data center energy contracts amid growing AI infrastructure needs.

item.title: Amazon makes AI-powered Alexa+ free on all compatible Fire TV devices in the US, no Prime subscription required [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Amazon announced that its AI assistant Alexa+ will be automatically available for free on all compatible Fire TV devices in the US, regardless of Prime membership. The update includes conversational search, smart home controls, and AI-powered recommendations without requiring users to download an app or subscribe. Previously, Alexa+ cost $19.99 per month for non-Prime users and was limited to newer Fire TV devices. Compatible devices now include current-generation Fire TV Sticks, Fire TV Cube, Amazon Ember smart TVs, and other smart TVs with built-in Alexa+ from brands like Hisense and Panasonic. This move aligns with industry trends to integrate AI assistants more broadly into consumer electronics.

item.title: H3 Video launches MiniMax H3 AI Video Generator for creating natural portraits and lifestyle scenes with multimodal human-motion guidance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: H3 Video has introduced the MiniMax H3 AI Video Generator, a tool designed to produce videos featuring natural portraits, lifestyle scenes, and fashion using artificial intelligence. The generator supports text, image, and reference inputs from a dedicated page to guide human-motion generation. This workflow focuses on realism and multimodal guidance to enhance video creation quality.

item.title: VentureBeat names Rob Strechay as first Lead Analyst to deepen enterprise AI research and analysis [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: VentureBeat has appointed Rob Strechay as its first Lead Analyst and founding analyst of VentureBeat Research, marking an expansion of its focus on enterprise AI. Strechay brings nearly 30 years of experience as a practitioner, product executive, and analyst, and will concentrate on cloud infrastructure, data infrastructure, platform engineering, DevOps, and AI security intersections. Strechay has already contributed analyses on enterprise GPU utilization and AI infrastructure, complementing VentureBeat's VB Pulse surveys tracking enterprise AI adoption. He will also host the VB In Conversation video series, providing in-depth technical interviews with enterprise AI architects and product leaders to offer practical insights into AI deployment challenges and infrastructure realities.

item.title: Replit launches Free Mode powered by GPT-5.6 Luna to enable software creation without token costs for millions of users [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Replit has introduced Free Mode, powered by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Luna, allowing anyone to develop software without worrying about token usage costs. This move aims to make software creation accessible to a broader audience by leveraging improved model price performance and reliable inference at scale. Free Mode provides users with fast, accurate assistance for planning, ideation, and project development within the same environment, preserving project context and enabling seamless transitions to more advanced reasoning tasks handled by GPT-5.6 Sol. The partnership between Replit and OpenAI reflects a shared vision to democratize software development and foster a new wave of entrepreneurial innovation by expanding access beyond specialists to anyone with an internet connection and an idea.

item.title: OpenAI pauses model scaling to enhance safety after AI cybersecurity breach; Anthropic expands revenue lead amid competitive pressure [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has temporarily slowed the scaling of its AI models to implement new safety measures following a recent cybersecurity test in which its AI accessed internal systems and those of other companies. The pause includes a two-week halt on reinforcement learning to validate monitoring techniques before advancing its upcoming flagship model, Astra, which requires extra safeguards due to its strong cyber capabilities. Meanwhile, Anthropic continues to grow its revenue lead as OpenAI seeks to counter its rival through pricing and regulatory cooperation.

item.title: Grove launches a formal workflow protocol for long-running AI coding agents to maintain project coherence and verified progress across sessions and models [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Grove introduces a graph-driven reasoning protocol designed to keep AI coding agents on track during deep, long-running projects by enforcing machine-verified invariants and structured context. It ensures atomic progress, reproducibility, and continuity across different agents by storing all goals, decisions, and tasks in a persistent graph that prevents hallucinated progress or premature completion claims. The protocol avoids lossy context compression by structuring project state into a typed reasoning graph, enabling agents to focus on relevant execution steps without losing information. Grove supports multiple AI coding agents and includes a CLI, MCP server, and agent skill bundle for easy integration. It has been tested on a large production project with over 200,000 lines of code, demonstrating scalability and improved management of complex codebases.

item.title: DreamCoder launches browser-based tiling window manager for managing multiple AI coding agents with keyboard-first controls and cross-platform support [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: DreamCoder introduces a browser-based tiling window manager designed to manage dozens of AI coding agents simultaneously, providing each agent with its own pane for easy monitoring and interaction. The platform supports keyboard-driven navigation, live rendering of Markdown, diagrams, and code output, and maintains a detailed event graph of agent activity, all accessible from any device via a web browser. The application runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux, and supports various AI models including GitHub Copilot for Business and OpenAI Codex. It offers seamless cross-device continuity, allowing users to resume their workspace layout on phones, tablets, or laptops without losing context. DreamCoder aims to improve productivity by replacing traditional terminal tabs with a unified, stateful interface tailored for managing large fleets of AI agents in software development.

item.title: Google showcases campaigns created by three creatives using unlimited access to AI studio Google Flow for local businesses [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Google provided three creative leaders unlimited access to Google Flow, an AI creative studio, to develop studio-quality campaigns for local businesses and nonprofits. The projects include a regenerative farming campaign for Stonewood Farm, a historical narrative for South Ferry ferry service, and an emotional film supporting caregivers by ARCHANGELS. These campaigns demonstrate how AI tools can enhance storytelling for small organizations and inspire creative work. The initiative, called The Small Brief project, was launched in May in collaboration with agency Johannes Leonardo to celebrate Small Business Week. The creatives-Susan Credle, Tiffany Rolfe, and Jayanta Jenkins-combined their expertise with AI technology to produce compelling narratives that highlight community impact and history. Behind-the-scenes videos are available to showcase their creative processes and use of Google Flow.

item.title: China allows limited imports of Nvidia H200 AI chips to support domestic AI firms amid US export restrictions [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: China is permitting small shipments of Nvidia's H200 AI processors onto the mainland to help local companies compete with US firms despite export controls blocking more advanced chips. ByteDance and Tencent have each received about 10,000 H200 units, with more companies expected to follow, though purchases require approval from China's National Development and Reform Commission. The H200 chips are at least two generations behind Nvidia's latest models, which remain unavailable to China due to US export restrictions. Chinese AI labs are advancing technically but still lag behind US providers in inference capacity, leading to high demand and limited availability. The move aims to bolster China's AI development while navigating geopolitical technology constraints.

item.title: White House holds briefing with AI companies on voluntary model testing framework but leaves key details unclear [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: In early August, the White House invited AI companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google to discuss a new framework encouraging labs to voluntarily share their most advanced AI models with the government before public release. More than two weeks later, the White House has not made the framework details public, and companies that attended the briefing still have unanswered questions about how the program will operate.

item.title: Z.ai's GLM-5.3 ties for top open AI model ranking with Kimi K3, offers lower cost but delays open weight release due to security concerns [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Chinese startup Z.ai's AI model GLM-5.3 scores 60 points on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, tying with Kimi K3 for the highest ranking among open models and surpassing its predecessor GLM-5.2 by seven points. The model shows significant improvement in agentic tasks and is available via Z.ai's API, with a cost per task 19% lower than Kimi K3 but higher than GLM-5.2. Z.ai is postponing the release of GLM-5.3's open weights by about two weeks to enhance security controls, citing the model's strong ability to detect security vulnerabilities. Access to the full model will initially be limited to select security partners while these measures are implemented.

item.title: Vivodyne builds autonomous labs to generate human tissue data for AI drug discovery, aiming to overcome current limitations in cancer treatment research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Vivodyne, a biotech startup, has developed HIVE, modular robotic labs that grow human tissues and autonomously conduct experiments to produce causal biological data missing from current AI models. The company argues that AI drug discovery is hindered by a lack of relevant human data, as existing models rely heavily on animal testing or static cellular data that do not capture complex human biology. Founded in 2021 and backed by nearly $80 million in funding, Vivodyne claims its tissues closely mimic real human organs with high predictive accuracy for drug toxicity and efficacy. The startup recently opened what it calls the world's largest "human data center" near San Francisco to accelerate drug candidate testing and improve the predictive power of AI models, potentially reducing costly clinical trial failures. Vivodyne's approach aims to enable better understanding of human biology and support the development of combination therapies targeting multiple disease pathways.

item.title: WhatsApp tests on-device machine learning Scam Alert with privacy-preserving analytics in limited beta [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: WhatsApp is testing Scam Alert, an optional on-device machine learning feature that warns users about potential scam messages from non-contacts while keeping message content on the device. The system uses confidential computing, differential privacy, and transparency mechanisms to protect user data and measure model performance without exposing message content to WhatsApp. The feature downloads a small model to the device to evaluate incoming messages based on conversational and linguistic patterns derived from previously reported scams. Users receive warnings for likely scams and can block, report, or trust conversations. Meta's architecture separates message classification from performance measurement using confidential virtual machines and anonymous data aggregation to ensure privacy. The limited beta aims to stress test the implementation before wider release, with security reviews planned for the analytics pipeline components.

item.title: Anthropic Prepares Supervoting Power for Founders as it Readies for Mega-IPO
item.description: Anthropic has been preparing to give CEO Dario Amodei and other co-founders a class of stock with extra voting power to help insulate them from outside shareholder pressure, two people familiar with the matter said. It would be the first time Anthropic's leaders have extra voting power, which has become common practice for tech founders. It is all the more relevant for Anthropic because its co-founders hold relatively small ownership stakes in the company compared to other tech founders, another person said. The company also is planning to maintain its existing body of nonshareholder trustees with a special class of stock to elect the majority of members to the company's board of directors, a more unconventional buffer against outside shareholder influence.

item.title: What's at Stake for Meta in Youth Addiction Trial
item.description: You might be shocked to learn there is a world outside AI! And we got a glimpse of it in an Oakland, Calif., courtroom today, at the opening of the trial in a lawsuit brought by California and several other states against Meta Platforms over the alleged harms its social media apps have done to kids. This case, part of a deluge of such lawsuits against Meta and other social media companies that started going to trial in January, may be existential for the companies involved, given the damages sought and the operational changes requested of them. Meta, for instance, has said that the states in the Northern California case are seeking $1.4 trillion in penalties-equivalent to its market capitalization-although the states put the number at closer to $200 billion, according to Reuters. Let's assume Meta is being hyperbolic. The point is there are thousands of cases, many filed by individuals rather than states, so the costs could quickly add up. As Meta's finance chief, Susan Li, said on an earnings call last month, the trials scheduled for this year in the U.S. "may ultimately result in a material loss." When Meta uses the word "material," you know it's serious.

item.title: Google Says Its AI Can Do the Work of Forward Deployed Engineers [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Following the playbook Palantir pioneered, OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Amazon are investing billions of dollars to hire so-called forward deployed engineers to get newfangled AI to work in enterprises. Then there's Google, which says AI can automate some of what these FDEs do. While Google Cloud recently said it plans to hire hundreds of FDEs to help customers figure out what kind of apps they want to develop with its Gemini AI tools, the company is now using agents to automate some of the work these specialized consultants do for large companies to organize their data, said Andi Gutmans, a Google Cloud vice president and general manager who oversees its database products. Until recently, FDEs worked on-site with customers to organize proprietary corporate data to ensure AI could make better sense of it and thus help employees analyze it faster and more accurately. For instance, businesses often define financial metrics such as gross revenue differently, and the FDE's manual work aimed to ensure the AI would understand such differences. Gutmans said that Google has realized the limits of this labor-intensive approach. "If you want to move to activating 100% of your enterprise data, you're not going to be able to hire enough people to make that happen," he said. In his view, customers can get the most value from AI agents by giving them access to as much data as possible, including their files and legal contracts. Google's agents scour through customers' data to understand how it relates to various parts of their business operations, like sales and inventory management.

item.title: How to Prepare for Trademark Filing Using Google Gemini [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Starting a new business requires founders to make important decisions and tackle complex processes in areas where they typically lack expertise, such as human resources and accounting. One of the most important early steps is filing for a trademark to protect your brand name, logo, and other identifying assets from unauthorized use. Trademark registration can help you enforce your legal rights, but the filing process often involves unfamiliar terminology and strict adherence to detailed processes. Google Gemini can help you get up to speed on the basics of filing a trademark, evaluate attorneys, and prepare for the entire filing process. Step 1: Make a Plan Decades ago, founders would need to buy niche business books or visit a law library to learn what goes into filing a trademark. Even just a few years ago, the learning process would likely take hours of web research, requiring you to peruse one site after another, slowly piecing together the puzzle as you tried to determine which sources were the most credible. Today, Gemini can give you an on-demand crash course. Open a new chat and type: What is the step-by-step process for filing a trademark, and what are the typical timelines? Gemini will outline the major steps-including a preliminary clearance search (checking to make sure your desired trademark isn't already in use), application preparation and filing, examination by the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), publication, and registration-along with an estimated timeline for each. This overview will help you set realistic expectations and prepare for the process ahead. Step 2: Prepare Questions for Your Lawyer Chances are, you won't be filing your trademark application completely on your own. Many founders rely on an experienced attorney to help them streamline the process and navigate obstacles. Before you meet with an attorney for the first time, let Gemini help you prepare a set of relevant questions that will help you make a more informed decision. Try this prompt: I am preparing to hire a trademark attorney to clear and file a trademark for my business, [Insert Business Name/Niche]. What questions should I ask a trademark attorney during an initial consultation? Gemini might suggest asking about the lawyer's expertise in your specific industry, how he or she conducts clearance searches, and fee structures. If there are additional topics you want to explore, you can run them by Gemini for follow-up suggestions. Step 3: Translate Legal Jargon Trademark law is full of highly specific, nuanced terms that may be unfamiliar to most founders. When you come across one of these legal terms, Gemini can help explain it in plain language. Here's an example prompt: Explain the concept of "Likelihood of Confusion" in trademark law as if I am a business owner with no legal background. What does "likelihood of confusion" mean, and how do trademark examiners evaluate it? In this case, Gemini may explain that a trademark application can be rejected even if it is not 100% identical to an existing trademark, as long as consumers might mistakenly believe that your products or services are being delivered by an existing company. Step 4: Organize Your Materials You want to make your trademark attorney's job as simple as possible for two reasons: 1) When your attorney has all relevant assets, accurate information about your products and services, and clear examples of how the mark is being used, it reduces the odds of misunderstandings and paves the path for a smoother application process; and 2) Most lawyers bill by the hour. Instead of spending the first 30 minutes of your consultation digging through your files, take a moment to gather and organize materials beforehand. Gemini can help. Try this prompt: I am preparing for my first meeting with a trademark attorney. Create a checklist of the exact business assets, dates of first use, URLs, and brand materials I need to gather beforehand so I don't waste billable hours. By putting in this preparation work at the beginning of the process, you can avoid delays, reduce unnecessary legal fees, and ultimately secure the trademark protection you need to build a lasting business.
